lane: P-101 ladder re-cut scope (read-only change inventory)

adversarialReviewOfMyOwnFindings.finding: hauska-map has no screens client code.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnFindings.firstMechanism: The PE workbench never shipped a screens surface; screens are a connector-only capability.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnFindings.competingMechanism: The client calls screens under a different path spelling, or through a generic proxy that does not name the path.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnFindings.howRejected: Two independent derivations. (1) git grep -n "property-explorer/v1/screens" origin/main in the hauska-map checkout exits 1. (2) The deep proxy is path-allowlisted in apps/property-explorer/api/_lib/deep-allowlist.ts and no screens path appears in DEEP_GET_EXACT, DEEP_GET_PREFIX, DEEP_POST_EXACT, SAVED_PROPERTY_ITEM_RE, or RECORDS_REQUEST_PURCHASE_RE; isDeepPathAllowed returns false for POST on anything not listed. A generic call would 403. These derive from different files by different authors.

adversarialReviewOfMyOwnFindings.finding: The three screen tools are ungated in the MCP.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnFindings.firstMechanism: No gate was ever written for them.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnFindings.competingMechanism: A gate exists upstream at the api-server route and the MCP inherits it, making a local gate unnecessary.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnFindings.howRejected: Not rejected — CONFIRMED as the second half. The api-server routes carry requirePeAuthenticated ONLY (propertyExplorer.ts:548, :576, :598, :626), so there is no upstream gate to inherit either. Both halves are open.

adversarialReviewOfMyOwnFindings.finding: Gating at the api-server route makes the MCP inherit the gate.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnFindings.firstMechanism: The MCP proxies to the same routes.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnFindings.competingMechanism: The MCP presents a service key and could bypass a user-scoped gate.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnFindings.howRejected: Read the impersonation path. peServiceUserId.ts requires SERVICE_API_KEY plus X-PE-User-Id, and resolvePeEntitlement then reads pe_user_entitlements for THAT user id from the database. The tier is never taken from a header. A route gate therefore evaluates the real subscriber tier on the MCP path too.

adversarialReviewOfMyOwnFindings.finding: The MCP suite would fail if the screen gate were added.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnFindings.firstMechanism: CORTEX_CALLS asserts each screen tool reaches cortex once.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnFindings.competingMechanism: The test fixture is already Studio, so a Studio gate passes and nothing fails.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnFindings.howRejected: The competing mechanism WINS. tools.test.ts:23-29 sets defaultAuth to accessTier paid / subscriptionTier studio. Every screen assertion runs as a Studio caller. My first reading was wrong; corrected before it reached the report.

correctionsMadeDuringWork: Initially assumed two subscriptionTierGrantsStudio copies per the dispatch. There are three, across two repos. Corrected.

Initially assumed the MCP CORTEX_CALLS tests would break under a new gate. They would not; the fixture is Studio. Corrected to the stronger and worse finding: adding the gate produces zero MCP test failures.

Initially assumed the dossier export kind is where the records package lives on every surface. On the PE side, dossier is the X-ray report and is NOT studio-gated; records is its own catalog entry (REC, engine records, studioGated true). The dispatch premise for item 3 holds on the MCP side only.
constraintsHonored: Read-only in both product repos. No checkout, stash, clean, fetch, or working-tree read.
No sub-agents spawned. No git write.
